audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 4 disagree with the mirror audit (maokai__warwick), which set Level 1 Warwick, Levels 2-3 Maokai, Levels 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Maokai, First item and 2+ items Warwick.
audit.why: The two directions must agree. Maokai owning levels 2-3 is also the kit-supported reading: Twisted Advance is a lock-on root at 14s rank 1 and Bramble Smash knocks you out of your own trade on a 7s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 4 flipped on both layers as one atomic group with matching ratings, and whys[1], whys[2], whys[4] and the mid prose rewritten so the text stops arguing the opposite of its own chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid prose calls levels 3-5 'your window' while the chart now gives him 2-3, and no spike carried a cooldown number.
audit.why: The window that survives is levels 4-5, played on his root cooldowns: Twisted Advance 14s at rank 1, Sapling Toss 18s at rank 1, Nature's Grasp 130s at rank 1 against your Infinite Duress at 110s.
audit.corrected: mid rewritten around the real window and the real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability slots are swapped throughout: spikes[0].text calls Sapling Toss '(Q)' and Bramble Smash '(W)', spikes[2].text and the late prose credit a 'passive sapling heal' and call the knockback his W, and spikes[3].text says 'his R root and W knockback'. On top of that, phases[4].why and breakdown.late call Infinite Duress a 'point-and-click fight starter'.
audit.why: Bramble Smash is Q — a 600-range shockwave that knocks back and slows, 7s at rank 1. Twisted Advance is W — a dash that makes him UNTARGETABLE and roots on arrival, 14s at rank 1. Sapling Toss is E, 1100 range, 18s at rank 1. Sap Magic is an attack heal refreshed whenever he casts or is struck by a spell — nothing to do with saplings. And Infinite Duress is a directional leap suppressing the first champion collided with for 1.5s.
audit.corrected: Every slot corrected, Sap Magic described as what it is, and the untargetable frame on Twisted Advance stated — it is the reason a level-6 leap can whiff entirely.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged "His Nature's Grasp" in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name.
audit.why: False positive — Nature's Grasp is Maokai's R.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Maokai's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion it hits for 1.5s, but Twisted Advance goes untargetable mid-dash and Nature's Grasp roots from 3000 range.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Maokai carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion in its path for 1.5s — his root goes first, so leap second. Maokai carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: Before Maokai stacks health you out-trade him: his Sapling Toss (Q) poke is mana-hungry and low, and your W-empowered Jaws plus Eternal Hunger sustain beats his Bramble Smash (W) knockback trade when his passive heal is on cooldown.
edits.after: Before Maokai stacks health you out-trade him: Sapling Toss (E, 18s at rank 1) is his only real poke, and your Blood Hunt Jaws plus Eternal Hunger beats the Bramble Smash (Q, 7s) knockback trade while Sap Magic is on cooldown.

edits.before: Once Maokai builds tank health his passive sapling heal and Bramble Smash scaling make his sustain match yours, and his W knockback plus root chains your engage; play around his cooldowns.
edits.after: Once Maokai builds health, Sap Magic — his attack heal, refreshed whenever spells are cast near him — matches your sustain, and Bramble Smash knocks you off while Twisted Advance roots you.

edits.before: Late Maokai is a peel machine — his R root and W knockback lock you off any carry, and his health stacking means your on-hit damage barely dents him, so he wins every extended fight.
edits.after: Late Maokai is a peel machine — Nature's Grasp roots and Bramble Smash knocks you back off any carry, and his health stacking blunts your on-hit damage, so he wins the extended fight.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your window — his health isn't stacked so W-empowered Jaws burst plus sustain out-trades him. At 6 it becomes a skill test around baiting his Nature's Grasp root.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 belong to him: Twisted Advance (14s at rank 1) roots you into Bramble Smash, and at 6 Nature's Grasp roots from across the lane — your window is levels 4-5, played on those cooldowns.

edits.before: Level 2 is a skill coin-flip before his kit and mana come online.
edits.after: Level 2 tilts to Maokai once Bramble Smash knocks you off.

edits.before: At 3 your W-empowered burst out-trades his low early health.
edits.after: At 3 his Twisted Advance root chains into a full trade.

edits.before: At 6 baiting his Nature's Grasp lets you win the skill fight with R.
edits.after: At 6 Nature's Grasp roots you out of the Duress leap entirely.

notes: Bramble Smash carries a 'grounding' derived flag that Riot's own text does not support — the description is only knockback, damage and slow. I treated the description as authoritative and made no grounding claim, the same call the mirror auditor made; worth resolving at champion level, because if the flag is right it changes every Maokai matchup against a dash champion. Also unresolved and unwritten: whether CC must land before the suppression applies to cancel Infinite Duress, or can break it mid-suppression.
